Main.sentence: The Profile in Courage Award is a private award created by the ___E:Kennedy family U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kennedy_family)___ to recognize displays of courage similar to those ___E:John F. Kennedy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy)___ originally described in his ___E:book of the same name U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Profiles_in_Courage)___ .

It is given to individuals (often elected officials) who, by acting in accord with their ___E:conscience U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conscience)___ , risked their careers or lives by pursuing a larger vision of the national, state or local interest in opposition to ___E:popular U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Popularity)___ opinion or pressure from constituents or other local interests.

The winners of the award are selected by a committee named by the ___E:John F. Kennedy Library Foundation U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Presidential_Library_and_Museum)___ , which includes members of the Kennedy family and other prominent Americans.

It is generally awarded each year around the time of JFK's birthday (May 29) at a ceremony at the ___E:Kennedy Library U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Fitzgerald_Kennedy_Library)___ in ___E:Boston U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Boston)___ .
The award is generally presented by JFK's daughter, ___E:Caroline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Caroline_Kennedy)___ .

Also before their deaths, other presenters had included John Kennedy's brother, ___E:Ted U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Kennedy)___ , his son ___E:John Jr. U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_F._Kennedy_Jr.)___ , and his widow ___E:Jacqueline U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacqueline_Kennedy_Onassis)___ .

Two recipients, ___E:John Lewis U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Lewis)___ (in 2001) and ___E:William Winter U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Winter_(politician))___ (in 2008), were designated as honorees for Lifetime Achievement.

The winner is presented with a ___E:sterling silver U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sterling_silver)___ ___E:lantern U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lantern)___ made by ___E:Tiffany's U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tiffany_%26_Co.)___ which was designed by ___E:Edwin Schlossberg U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Edwin_Schlossberg)___ .

The lantern is patterned after the lanterns on the USS Constitution which was launched in 1797. It is the last sail-powered ship to remain part of the ___E:US Navy U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Navy)___ , and is permanently moored nearby.
The awards were accepted by ___E:Cho Hyun-dong U:(https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cho_Hyun-dong)___ (South Korea) and Takeo Mori and Kotaro Suzuki (Japan).
